gen-gf-source-code-pro-fs-bespoke-sans: Sharp and refined, with curves that stop well short of the stem, the body text feels crisp. Bespoke Sans is the quiet star here, because Source Code Pro's typewriter regularity gives its finer drawing something rigid to lean against.
gen-gf-stack-sans-headline-fs-karma: Karma is a text serif with a settled, trustworthy look, its light strokes receding only slightly. Karma's gentle modulation sits under Stack Sans Headline's glassy, tube-like lines, so the headings glow while the paragraphs stay quietly readable.
gen-gf-syne-mono-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern and open, its c tips holding well apart and its mean line set high. And Syne Mono's cut-out, router-bit strokes make it feel like a machine part set beside something more human.
gen-gf-the-girl-next-door-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab carries the dignity, built low and compact. The Girl Next Door is graceful and personal with its broad hooked c, while Trench Slab does the steadier work of holding a line together.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-cossette-titre: Commanding in its heading, this pair leans on Tilt Neon's tube-like stroke and large x-height. And Cossette Titre answers with open bowls and tightly nestled letters, which gives the whole thing a strong, unified texture.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Noto Sans Thaana reads approachable and open. Its strongest quality is the way those wide, welcoming counters soften Tilt Neon's cut-ribbon strokes and splayed c, which would otherwise feel very forceful.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-strait: Strait draws big round lowercase bowls that feel friendly and contemporary. And Tilt Neon's wirelike strokes of one thickness keep a long passage lively, since the body sits low in contrast and rarely tires the eye.
gen-gf-train-one-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, with generous openings in every curve. Train One's drawn-out, wirelike cadence is the strongest single quality, because its expressive heading lines sit against Rowan's thin strokes at half the weight of its thick ones.
gen-gf-ubuntu-mono-fs-erode: Squat, wide and strictly structured, the headings arrive first. Erode's tall middle band and gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight bring a dignified editorial warmth that Ubuntu Mono, with no hairlines at all, wholly lacks.
gen-gf-ubuntu-mono-work-sans: Ubuntu Mono keeps its stems and curves uniform and open-ended, with a wide-looking lowercase and squat ascenders that feel structured. Work Sans does the contemporary part, with c tips that never creep toward touching and a mean line set high.
